pairs.reason: Navy surface with a cyan second hero line and monospace display type carries the brand; the other version is near-black neutral with a grey half-headline that reads as disabled.
Light mode keeps the brand blue in the hero, with a strong primary CTA and a legible second line; the other has a grey second line and no brand colour.
Mobile hero keeps the navy and cyan identity with a clear, high-contrast hierarchy; the other is greyer and its secondary line is faint.
Navy docs surface and monospace headings suit an infrastructure product, and the cyan active nav is clearer; the other is flat near-black.
The monospace heading voice matches the CLI-centric product and the code blocks, and the blue-tinted light palette is consistent.
Monospace headings stay legible on a phone and keep identity, though the title wraps; the sans version is only marginally calmer.
Navy surface gives the tables and inline code better tonal separation, and the monospace headings tie the page to the product; the other blends into near-black.
Distinctive monospace headings keep a clear hierarchy, with a consistent blue link and active-nav treatment.
The CLI reference in navy with a cyan active item and a mono title feels native, and its code block separates from the page better.
Mobile prose on a navy ground with the brand mark and mono headings has clearer identity, and the diagram sits comfortably in the layout.

findings.problem: Wide monospace display type wraps the headline to three lines and the cyan second sentence is as heavy as the first, so the hero is tall and the emphasis is unclear.
findings.fix: Reduce the h1 size or tighten the tracking so it fits two lines. Keep cyan only on the key phrase.

findings.location: Break it. See it. Undo it. section
findings.problem: The four steps in the left column are tall and sparse, and the demo terminal on the right ends early, leaving an empty block below it. Step 4 is boxed as active while the others are not, with no clear active-state logic.
findings.fix: Make the steps a compact list that sticks beside the terminal. Highlight the active step in sync with the demo.

findings.problem: The diagram labels are about 10px monospace and low-contrast, and the panel is mostly empty space, so the layers and the A/M/D chips are hard to read.
findings.fix: Scale the diagram up, bring labels to at least 12px with higher-contrast text, and trim the padding.

findings.problem: The diagram shrinks until its labels are illegible, and the demo terminal's first line is clipped under the header (the "--wait" fragment).
findings.fix: Show a simplified diagram on mobile and scroll the terminal body from the top. Alternatively, stack the labels beside the layers.

findings.problem: Commands and comments are cut off at the right edge with no visible scroll cue or wrap, so `--description` strings and flags can't be read or copied with confidence.
findings.fix: Soft-wrap code on narrow widths or add a fade and scrollbar cue, and add a copy button to the frame.

findings.problem: The decorative three-dot title bar is empty and adds height, and the block has no visible copy button or language label. The tinted background is also close to the page surface.
findings.fix: Replace the dots with a label such as 'shell' plus a copy button. Strengthen the border or contrast against the page.

findings.problem: The CLI help is a single unstyled pre block. The long flag descriptions are clipped on the right (the --timeout and --output lines), and there is no section anchor, so users can't scan Flags or Examples or link to them.
findings.fix: Parse the sections into headings and a flag table with wrapping. Give the examples their own copyable blocks.

findings.problem: The price table sets the two region columns in monospace beside a proportional heading, and the section tables have different widths (the 1040px and 1193px tables against the full-width one), so the right edges don't align.
findings.fix: Use one table width for all tables. Put the numeric columns in tabular figures and the units in a caption.

findings.problem: The sidebar ends abruptly at about 900px, leaving a mismatched dark block beside the longer page, and the reference list is cut off mid-item ('spin trust') with no scroll indication.
findings.fix: Make the sidebar sticky and full height with its own scroll and a fade at the clipping edge.

findings.problem: The experimental banner sits in a bright teal band on every page, directly under the 'On this page' bar, and competes with the page title. The 'On this page' toggle and the banner are also stacked, which eats vertical space.
findings.fix: Make it a slimmer neutral strip with a warning icon, or dismissible, and merge the toggle row into the header on desktop.

findings.problem: Bright blue underlined links appear in every paragraph beside tinted inline-code chips. In the Linux requirements list the chips are dense, with uneven padding and heavy visual noise.
findings.fix: Tone down the link underline and use one chip style with consistent padding and a lower-contrast fill.

findings.location: Light-mode primary CTA and secondary button
findings.problem: Evaluate Spinbox is a small solid button with a barely visible outline secondary beside it. Both are small for a landing CTA, and the secondary lacks an affordance.
findings.fix: Increase the button size and padding and give the secondary a clear border. Use the same CTA treatment on dark and light.

pairs.reason: More disciplined type scale and denser lower-page composition make the landing page easier to scan while retaining the infrastructure-product character.
The stronger mono display treatment and higher-contrast terminal create a more distinctive, credible technical landing page.
On mobile, the cyan emphasis makes the central product promise materially clearer than the low-contrast secondary headline in b.
Mono headings establish a clearer documentation identity without compromising the readable prose and code structure.
The branded heading treatment gives the light documentation page stronger hierarchy and parity with dark mode.
The compact single-line title preserves valuable narrow-screen space and improves document scanning.
The sans-serif headings and tighter vertical rhythm make a data-heavy cost page easier to read.
Mono section headings make this overview feel purpose-built for operators rather than like generic documentation.
The wider, more consistently framed command-reference content improves scanning of the long CLI output.
The mono heading system better connects the mobile documentation page to Spinbox’s technical identity.

findings.problem: The muted gray “Keep control of what it changes” is part of the primary promise but recedes too far relative to the white first clause.
findings.fix: Use the cyan brand emphasis or a higher-contrast blue-white tone for the second clause; reserve muted text for supporting copy.

findings.problem: The large vertical gaps weaken continuity from the value proposition into proof and then into the workflow.
findings.fix: Reduce both section gaps and use a consistent section rhythm so the interactive demo reads as direct evidence for the headline.

findings.problem: Command text is rendered in very pale blue on a pale surface, making commands less legible than surrounding prose.
findings.fix: Increase code foreground contrast substantially and keep syntax color only for semantic tokens, not the entire command.

findings.location: Mobile “Break it. See it. Undo it.” section
findings.problem: The terminal demo is shown before the explanatory steps, reversing the learning sequence on the narrow layout.
findings.fix: Show the step list first, or interleave each step with the relevant terminal state before presenting the full transcript.

findings.problem: Several prose paragraphs and tables approach an overly wide reading measure for dense operational material.
findings.fix: Constrain prose and standard tables to a narrower content measure; let wide code examples opt into a wider overflow container.

findings.problem: Long commands visibly clip at the right edge, with no apparent horizontal-scroll affordance.
findings.fix: Provide an obvious horizontal scrolling treatment with a fade/scroll cue and a copy control; preserve command text without destructive wrapping.

findings.problem: The command lines are clipped horizontally, so essential arguments cannot be read or copied reliably.
findings.fix: Make code blocks horizontally scrollable with visible affordance, or provide per-line copy and carefully wrap explanatory—not executable—content.

findings.problem: The scenario table relies on desktop width without a visible small-screen treatment, making its four-column comparison fragile.
findings.fix: Define a responsive table pattern: retain scenario and price, stack or disclose the descriptive column, and preserve column headers.

findings.problem: The preformatted reference text runs beyond the visible right edge, hiding flag descriptions.
findings.fix: Use a horizontally scrollable code/reference container with an explicit scroll cue and copy affordance; avoid clipping overflow.

findings.problem: The diagram is scaled down until labels and relationships are not usable, despite being central to the page’s explanation.
findings.fix: Use a responsive diagram with a legible mobile composition, or supply a tap-to-expand full-resolution view and concise adjacent legend.

pairs.reason: The smaller two-line headline puts the diagram and demo higher on the screen. The primary and secondary buttons both read as buttons, and the blue primary has stronger contrast.
In the light theme the compact hero keeps the headline and CTAs in proportion. Both CTAs are clear buttons, and the diagram sits closer to the fold.
On the phone the headline takes three lines instead of five, and the full-width button pair is easier to tap. The diagram is visible sooner.
The code blocks sit on a lighter navy surface that separates them from the page. The page title is in better proportion to the h2s, and the syntax colours are more varied.
The page title is better proportioned to the h2s, and the layout is tighter. The prose measure and code styling are otherwise the same as in a.
The smaller title and tighter header spacing show more content above the fold. Everything else is the same as a.
The title is in better proportion to the section headings, and the logo sits on a tile that keeps it visible against the dark navy. The cost table is easier to scan.
The h1 and h2 scale is more restrained, so more of the prose and the nav cards fit on screen. The reading rhythm is the same as in a.
The CLI help block is on a more distinct navy surface, and the title is in better proportion. Both versions clip long lines at the right edge.
The h1 and h2 sizes are better matched to the body text on a narrow screen. Everything else is the same as in a.

findings.location: CLI reference pre block, the --timeout and --output flag rows
findings.problem: Long flag descriptions run off the right edge of the block and are clipped, with no wrapping or scroll indicator. Descriptions are lost in the reference the audience relies on most.
findings.fix: Wrap long lines in the generated help block with a hanging indent, or add a visible horizontal scroll affordance.

findings.location: Code blocks on mobile ('Taking one', 'Going back')
findings.problem: Commands are cut at the right edge (`--description "bei`, `--wa`). They can only be read by horizontal scrolling, and nothing signals that. The window-chrome dots take space and add no meaning.
findings.fix: Add a fade or scroll shadow on the overflow edge, and a copy button on every block. Drop the dots, or let long commands wrap with a continuation indent.

findings.problem: The sidebar surface ends abruptly at about y=900, while the page continues. This leaves a visible seam at the bottom of the nav column on long pages.
findings.fix: Make the sidebar background extend the full viewport height, or remove its distinct background.

findings.location: Light theme, code blocks and active nav item
findings.problem: The code surface is a cool grey-blue slab. The active sidebar item uses a saturated pale-blue fill with weak label contrast. Both blend with the banner colour and make the light theme feel washed out next to the dark theme.
findings.fix: Use a near-white code surface with a 1px border. Switch the active nav item to a thin cyan or navy marker with a navy label.

findings.location: Dark terminal inside the light hero
findings.problem: A heavy near-black demo panel in the light theme overpowers the headline and breaks the light/dark parity. The light hero also carries two tinted bands (banner and diagram panel) at similar weight.
findings.fix: Give the light theme a light terminal surface, or keep the terminal dark and tone down the banner. Make both themes use one token for code surfaces.

findings.problem: The diagram has large empty margins and tiny mono labels, about 10px. Its right half repeats the diff command and result, which the demo panel below shows again, and a gap sits between the diff text and the step chips.
findings.fix: Scale the diagram and its labels up, or crop the panel to its content. Remove the duplicated diff text, or show one demo in one place.

findings.problem: The diagram labels shrink to illegible size (about 6px) on the phone, so the diagram reads as decoration.
findings.fix: Show a simplified vertical stack on narrow screens with labels at 12px or larger, or put the labels beneath the diagram.

findings.location: 'Break it. See it. Undo it.' section
findings.problem: Four steps sit in a narrow left column against a demo panel with dead space beneath it. The step headings wrap badly ('Take a snapshot, memory and / all'), and only step 04 is boxed.
findings.fix: Make the steps one even row or a stacked list with consistent boxing. Fix the heading widths. Put the demo panel in a sticky column or shorten it to match.

findings.problem: The first lines of the terminal are clipped at the top (`--wait` is visible alone). The block cuts content without a scroll cue, and commands wrap mid-flag, which makes them hard to copy and read.
findings.fix: Size the container to its content, or start the scroll at the top. Wrap with a hanging indent at flag boundaries.

findings.problem: The first table spans the full measure, but the next two stop at about 65 to 75% of it, each at a different width. Column widths and row heights are inconsistent across the page. The inline code chips in the settings table sit tight against the row rules.
findings.fix: Give all tables the same width and the same first-column treatment. Add vertical padding to code chips in table cells.

findings.problem: The mono 'Installations run Spinbox…' provenance line is small, low in contrast and has the same weight as the links inside it. The pagination cards use a large title face compared with the body text.
findings.fix: Set the provenance line in the muted text token at 12px with a stronger link colour. Reduce the pagination title to the h4 size.

findings.location: h1 and h2 headings in the monospace display face
findings.problem: Wide mono headings at a large size wrap quickly and eat vertical space in prose pages. On mobile, 'Snapshots and rollback' breaks into two lines. Headings look the same as code, which weakens the distinction between prose and commands.
findings.fix: Use a proportional face for h1 to h3 and keep mono for code, ids and eyebrows. Otherwise cut the h2 size by about 15% and use tighter tracking.

findings.problem: The banner sits on every page, takes about 40px of fixed header space, and uses a bold teal-tinted fill that competes with the cyan CTA. On mobile it takes two lines.
findings.fix: Make the banner a thin muted strip with a single line, or let it be dismissed. Use a neutral surface so cyan stays reserved for actions.

pairs.reason: The three-line hero preserves a clearer reading rhythm and gives the primary action more deliberate emphasis.
The headline wraps naturally rather than forcing the cyan clause into a visually crowded two-line lockup.
The mobile hero has more consistent CTA hierarchy and breathing room.
The larger page title creates a more legible documentation hierarchy without compromising the content column.
The title and section hierarchy are clearer while retaining a calm, documentation-first density.
The mobile heading scale is more distinct from body prose and section headings.
It better balances the page title against the substantive table and reading content.
The page title is less oversized, keeping the long evaluation document focused on its content.
The stronger command-page title makes the reference hierarchy easier to scan.
Both versions provide effectively the same clear mobile reading structure and visual hierarchy.

findings.problem: The first visible terminal line begins with “--wait”, making the command sequence look vertically clipped and breaking the demo narrative.
findings.fix: Ensure the terminal transcript starts at its first command on narrow layouts; allow its height to expand or use an intentional scroll container with a visible overflow cue.

findings.problem: Long commands are visibly cut off at the right edge with no horizontal-scroll affordance or wrapping strategy.
findings.fix: Make code blocks horizontally scrollable with a persistent fade/scroll cue, or selectively wrap command examples while retaining copyable unwrapped source.

findings.location: Mobile landing-page “Break it. See it. Undo it.” section
findings.problem: The terminal precedes the explanatory step cards, so the command output arrives before users understand the workflow it demonstrates.
findings.fix: On narrow screens, place the compact step explanation before the terminal, or add a clearly labeled workflow summary immediately above it.

findings.problem: Desktop body copy spans a broad content area, producing lines that are long for sustained technical reading.
findings.fix: Constrain prose to roughly 68–75ch while allowing tables and code samples to use a wider overflow-capable container.

findings.problem: The hamburger exposes navigation but there is no visible current-section or in-page progress signal once the sidebar is collapsed.
findings.fix: Retain a compact current-page/current-heading indicator beneath the top bar, linked to the expanded navigation.

findings.location: Cost tables on dark documentation pages
findings.problem: Table rules and secondary labels are muted enough that scanning rows and associating region prices requires more effort than necessary.
findings.fix: Increase row-divider and muted-label contrast slightly, while preserving cyan only for links and active states.

findings.problem: The fourth “Roll back” card is visually isolated below the three-step list, weakening the intended sequence.
findings.fix: Use a four-step grid at wide widths or connect the final card to the prior steps with an explicit continuation treatment.

pairs.reason: Headline sets in two lines without the orphaned 'changes.', and the solid primary plus bordered secondary button read as a clear pair. The hero is shorter, so the demo shows sooner.
The headline breaks cleanly in two lines and the solid blue primary beside a bordered secondary reads as two buttons. The hero is more restrained, and the mono eyebrow is not needed.
On a phone the headline takes three lines and not four, and both CTAs sit side by side as real buttons. The demo terminal comes sooner and there is less scrolling.
Smaller h1 and h2 with tighter gaps give more prose per screen, and the headings still stand out from the body. The oversized mono h2s in the other version crowd the 960px measure.
The calmer heading scale suits documentation better. More content is visible per screen, and the code blocks and the prose around them keep a steadier rhythm.
The title fits on one line at 390px and the section headings are proportionate. The other version wraps the h1 to two lines and spends vertical space on oversized headings.
The scenario and settings tables sit closer to their headings, so the cost data reads sooner. The heading scale is proportionate to the table text.
Moderate headings keep the page prose-led and let it fit on fewer screens. The oversized mono h2s in the other version compete with the body text.
Long flag descriptions wrap, so no text is clipped and no horizontal scroll is needed. The other version cuts off 'control plane gives…' and the default values at the right edge.
The h1 stays on one line and the h2s are proportionate. The prose measure is unchanged and more of the architecture text fits on screen.

findings.problem: The sidebar background ends at about 900px, and its nav list is clipped mid-item ('spin trust') on the CLI pages. Below that the page shows a different surface, so the column looks cut off. This appears on s04, s07 and s09, in dark and in light.
findings.fix: Make the sidebar full viewport height with sticky positioning and the page background. Let the nav scroll inside it.

findings.problem: The help text is one big preformatted block with flag columns aligned by spaces. Long descriptions wrap back to column 0 and break the alignment. There is no copy button, and flags and examples are not separate elements.
findings.fix: Render examples in normal code blocks with copy buttons. Render flags as a two-column table or definition list with a hanging indent, and keep the usage line as its own block.

findings.location: Code blocks on mobile (Taking one, Going back)
findings.problem: Commands are clipped at the right edge (the description string, '--wait', '--with-memory'). Nothing signals that the block scrolls, and the blocks have no copy button.
findings.fix: Add a visible scroll affordance (edge fade) and a copy button in the frame. Consider wrapping with a hanging indent below 480px.

findings.problem: The terminal's first line is cut off at the top ('--wait' alone) and the box has no title context. The diagram labels (running · writes here, snapshot · after) are tiny and unreadable at 390px.
findings.fix: Start the terminal at the first command, or size it to its content. Enlarge the labels or move them below the stack in a legend. Raise the minimum SVG text size to about 11–12px.

findings.problem: The right column leaves a large empty gap between the diff output and the step chips. The diagram and the code are different sizes and do not align on a baseline. The tiny 10px mono labels have weak contrast on the dark panel.
findings.fix: Use a grid with aligned top and bottom edges. Fill or remove the gap. Raise the label size to 12px and the colour to the secondary text token.

findings.location: Feature list '01 Snapshot … 04 Roll back' beside terminal
findings.problem: Card 04 has a box and 01–03 do not, so the selected state looks arbitrary. Titles orphan a word ('memory and / all', 'never / happened'). The 'How we know' links are about 11px underlined and stand out too little. The terminal column ends well short of the list.
findings.fix: Show the box only as an active-step state tied to the demo, or give all items one treatment. Set titles with text-wrap: balance. Make the links 13px and use a neutral colour until hover.

findings.problem: The us-east-1 and us-west-2 columns carry identical figures ($50, $418, $1,575). The table has no emphasis on the totals, and the numbers are not set in a tabular mono face. The 'All the time' and 'Settings' tables use a different width, so the page has three table widths.
findings.fix: Show one price column with a region note, or show the difference. Use tabular-nums and mono for figures. Give the tables one width and a consistent first-column weight.

findings.problem: The code frame has an empty chrome bar with three faint dots and a flat pale-blue body. Comment text and the --flag tokens are low-contrast, below AA on the pale blue. The dots carry no function and a language or filename label would be more useful. The dark hero terminal is a different treatment from the docs code blocks.
findings.fix: Drop the dots, or replace them with a shell label plus a copy button. Darken the comment and option tokens to at least 4.5:1. Use one code-block surface across hero and docs.

findings.problem: The full-width teal/blue band is the most saturated surface on every page, in both themes, and competes with the page title. It repeats on every screen. It is a status message but uses the brand cyan colour, so it does not read as a warning.
findings.fix: Make it a thin, dismissible neutral strip with an amber or status-coloured marker. Keep the brand cyan for interactive elements.

findings.location: Sidebar top-level tabs and 'On this page' bar
findings.problem: The icon tiles for Docs, Install, Security and Reference carry icons in coloured squares, and the active one is a bright cyan tile. They are heavier than the page links below. The 'On this page' bar and the breadcrumb 'Overview' have small, unaligned controls.
findings.fix: Use plain monoline icons and mark the active tab with a left rule and text colour. Align the TOC trigger height with the search field.

findings.problem: Inline code chips on the pale grey-blue sit close to the link colour. Links inside lists are underlined at weight equal to body, so many underlined phrases per paragraph make dense runs hard to scan.
findings.fix: Give inline code a clear surface and a 1px border. Use a slightly heavier link colour with a thin underline offset.

findings.problem: The two-colour mono headline ('Keep control of what it changes.') runs in cyan over a large block of the hero. The eyebrow 'spin-stack · self-hosted sandboxes' is a small low-contrast line. Together the hero says little about AWS or the product name.
findings.fix: Colour only 'what it changes' in cyan. Strengthen the eyebrow with the product name or a version, and keep it at least 13px.

findings.problem: The AWS diagram is shrunk to full width at 390px and every label is illegible. It is a white image on a dark page, so it is glaring and not in the theme. It has no tap-to-zoom.
findings.fix: Link the image to a full-size view (lightbox or open in new tab). Offer a dark variant or a muted frame, and add a text list of the parts as an alternative.

pairs.reason: The headline’s line breaks preserve the two-part message: the cyan promise reads as one deliberate unit.
The two-line desktop headline is materially more compact while retaining a clear reading order.
It uses the narrow viewport more efficiently: the main statement stays to three lines rather than fragmenting the first sentence.
No meaningful visible difference in hierarchy, readability, or layout.
No meaningful visible difference in hierarchy, readability, or layout.

The slightly tighter vertical rhythm makes the long operational cost document easier to scan.
Both establish the same strong documentation hierarchy and readable measure.
The reference content is set in a marginally more contained reading column, which better suits a very wide CLI output block.
Both provide the same clear, mobile-first technical-document layout.

findings.problem: “Install on AWS” is visually too close to plain supporting text in the preferred dark variant, despite being a primary evaluation path.
findings.fix: Use a quiet outlined secondary button with the same height, padding, and focus treatment as the primary CTA.

findings.problem: The large gap after the demo panel makes the first explanatory workflow feel detached from the product demonstration.
findings.fix: Reduce the section spacing one step or introduce a short transition label that links the demo to the workflow.

findings.problem: The terminal appears before the explanatory steps, unlike the desktop split layout; users encounter dense commands before the task context.
findings.fix: On narrow screens, place the selected step summary above the terminal or add a persistent step indicator immediately above it.

findings.problem: Long command lines are horizontally clipped with no visible wrapping, scrolling affordance, or copy control.
findings.fix: Provide a horizontally scrollable code region with a visible edge/fade affordance and a copy button; preserve unwrapped commands.

findings.problem: The table relies on dense prose in the “What runs” column and weakly separated monetary columns, making cross-region comparison slow.
findings.fix: Strengthen header/column alignment and use a narrower scenario description or responsive stacked row treatment before the table becomes cramped.

findings.problem: The article’s wide desktop measure approaches the upper comfortable limit for dense prose, especially in the opening explanatory paragraphs.
findings.fix: Cap prose content closer to 70–75ch while allowing tables and code blocks to use a wider overflow container.

findings.problem: The long generated reference lines visibly run into or beyond the panel edge, impairing command and flag readability.
findings.fix: Make the command reference block horizontally scrollable, retain full monospace lines, and expose a clear horizontal-scroll affordance.

findings.problem: The diagram is technically visible but too small to convey the relationships described in the adjacent text.
findings.fix: Open the image in a zoomable lightbox or provide a simplified mobile-specific diagram with readable labels.
